raw_response:
I will keep this year simple and steady. I am 67, so I do not want to chase crops that need too much labor, too much market judgment, or too much hand work. In Quzhou County, the land, water, and machines around me fit the usual wheat and summer maize rotation best, and I know how to manage it. That gives me food grain, stable sales, and lower risk than trying vegetables, cotton, or other cash crops. I will use improved or hybrid seed because I want reliable emergence, uniform growth, and better yield, but I will not make the management too complicated.

For the winter season, I will keep winter wheat on my land and manage it in the familiar way: one good basal fertilizer, then topdressing nitrogen when the crop needs it, irrigation only at the key stages, and pesticide only when disease or insects are likely to reduce yield. After wheat harvest, I will quickly plant summer maize so I do not lose soil moisture or miss the season. For maize, I will use hybrid seed, give enough nitrogen for strong growth, keep phosphorus and potassium moderate, and irrigate only if rainfall is not enough. I will use rotary tillage because it is easier for me, fits local machine work, and lets me turn the season around quickly between wheat harvest and maize sowing. My goal is not the highest possible yield. My goal is a crop plan I can actually finish well, with stable output and manageable labor.
